nodes.body: Front-buffer BO allocation ignores the same modifier/protected-content handling used for back buffers. On modifier-backed surfaces (or when ProtectedContent is set), creating the front BO via plain gbm_bo_create() can yield an incompatible/unprotected BO compared to the back/presented buffers.

The multipass draw overrides fragment sampler views/states for pass B but does not restore the previous sampler bindings afterward. The “non-array” check is ineffective for arrays-of-images because glsl_without_array(var->type) strips the outer array. This can incorrectly accept `image2D imgs[N]` even though the comment/spec says the predicate only admits a single non-array image.

The predicate doesn’t validate the stored value shape (components/write mask/bit size) or that the 2D coordinate has the expected 2 components. Without these checks, kernels that can’t be lowered to a single RGBA8 RT export may still be marked rt-exportable.

The coordinate gate reuses store_ssbo_addr_src_is_supported(), but that walker currently treats nir_intrinsic_load_vulkan_descriptor as supported (see store_ssbo_addr_def_is_supported). That means the “gid-derived only” requirement described in the header isn’t actually enforced for image coordinates.

This new public detector has several non-trivial acceptance rules but no unit coverage alongside the existing compute-admission NIR tests. Adding a couple of targeted tests (one positive, a few negatives like wrong format / extra store / array image / partial write mask) would help keep future lowering work from regressing the predicate.

If util_pstipple_create_sampler_view or util_pstipple_create_sampler fails (or returns NULL), the context ends up with a partially-initialized stipple setup and will never retry creation on subsequent calls (because pstipple_tex is now non-NULL and the code only updates the texture). nir_lower_pstipple_fs computes and returns the binding it chose via samplerUnitOut, but the result is currently written into a local `stipple_unit` and then ignored. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate the texture cache after stipple updates**

When `glPolygonStipple` changes between two stippled draws, this updates the already-bound `pstipple_tex` in place but only dirties `textures_state` below; no `texture_cache_inval` atom is emitted, unlike a normal `set_sampler_views` texture change. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-merge stipple texture when the fragment shader changes**

When polygon stipple stays enabled across a fragment-shader bind, this transition check does not run, but the injected texture slot is derived from the current FS's sampler bindings. A switch from a shader whose stipple unit is 1 to one whose unit is 2 leaves `textures_state` clean and keeps the hardware state at the old slot, while the newly picked stipple variant samples the new slot; that draw then samples an app texture or NULL instead of the stipple mask.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebuild SWTCL layout for the injected WPOS input**

On no-TCL chips, this lowering adds a `gl_FragCoord` read, which `nir_to_rc` records as `inputs.wpos`; however the pstipple transition only dirties textures/FS state, not `rs_block_state`. For a stippled draw whose original FS did not already read `gl_FragCoord`, the SWTCL vertex layout is not rebuilt to route WPOS, so the new variant reads an unassigned fragment input and the stipple lookup uses garbage coordinates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply stipple to fill faces under mixed polygon modes**

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count sampler arrays before choosing the stipple unit**

**suggestion:** Docstring mentions feature surfaces and tags, but the implementation only audits driver lists.

`parse_profile`/`audit` currently only read and enforce `gallium-drivers` and `vulkan-drivers`. If tags and feature surfaces are intended to be enforced, they should be validated (e.g., `tag` against allowed values / additional keys). Otherwise, consider updating the docstring to describe only what is actually checked to avoid implying broader coverage.

```suggestion
"""Fail when a build profile enables a driver its allowlist row forbids.

Each profile config under build-infra/configs/ (and configs/alternates/)
must have a row in build-infra/component-policy/radeon-minimal-allowlist.toml
naming its allowed gallium-drivers and vulkan-drivers. The audit parses
the meson-format config, compares the selected drivers against the row,
and exits nonzero on any driver outside the allowlist or any config file
without a row. Policy lives in the rows: the r300 release row omits zink,
the terakan rows carry the software rasterizers their x130e reference
runs compare against. The deprecated amd_r300 selector alias warns until
its removal branch lands.
"""
```

The module docstring is out of sync with the allowlist it points to: it says the r300 release row omits zink and that the policy covers "feature surfaces", but the TOML allowlist permits zink in every row and only defines gallium-drivers/vulkan-drivers (+ tag). This can mislead future edits of the policy gate.

The deprecated selector alias handling skips the allowlist check entirely (it `continue`s), so a profile selecting amd_r300 will pass even if the row does not permit the canonical ati_r300. It should warn but still enforce the allowlist using the canonical name.

`parse_profile()` uses `raw.strip("[]")` without trimming surrounding whitespace first. If the value ever acquires leading/trailing whitespace (or comes from a different formatting style), the leading `[`/trailing `]` won't be removed and the audit can report false violations. Stripping whitespace first makes the parser more robust.

The new `profile-audit` target is added as a gate, but it is not listed in the `help` output targets list. Since this is meant to be a runbook-cited gate, it should be discoverable via `make -C build-infra help`.

The audit should treat an absent selector as Meson’s effective default, or fail closed until the selector is explicit.

**issue:** Guard against empty `defined_in` to avoid accidentally adding the repo root (`.`) to the allowlist.

Because `target.get("defined_in", "")` can be empty, `os.path.realpath("")` resolves to the current working directory. If that matches `repo_root`, `add()` will add `"."` to `keep`, which is likely an invalid allowlist entry. Consider only calling `add()` when `defined_in` is truthy, e.g. `path = target.get("defined_in"); if path: add(path)`.

`--repo-root` defaults to ".", so the allowlist generation depends on the current working directory. If this script is invoked from a build directory (a common workflow when working with Meson), `repo_root` will point at the build tree and almost all source paths will be filtered out, producing an incorrect (often empty) allowlist and misleading "candidate prune surface" output. Default the repo root by inferring it from `__file__`, matching the existing style in `profile_audit.py`.

`add()` calls `os.path.realpath(path)` even when `path` is empty/falsey (e.g., `target.get("defined_in", "")`). In Python, `realpath("")` resolves to the current working directory, so depending on where the script is run this can accidentally add a directory like `build-infra/scripts` to the allowlist and skew the top-level reachability summary. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject vector-sized ALU offset nodes before chasing**

When a candidate offset contains a horizontal/vector ALU op such as `fdot`/`fdph` under an integer conversion, this loop calls `nir_scalar_chase_alu_src`, whose contract asserts that sized ALU inputs have size 1; in debug builds that turns an otherwise rejectable non-identity/non-binary shader into an assertion failure, and in release builds it only follows swizzle[0], ignoring the remaining vector lanes. The new walker should return false for ALU ops whose inputs are not scalar-safe before chasing them, so trying the detector on unsupported SSBO address expressions stays conservative.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match lowered compute system-value roots**

For Terakan Vulkan compute shaders, `terakan_shader.c` runs `nir_lower_system_values` and `nir_lower_compute_system_values` before `nir_lower_explicit_io`, and with `has_cs_global_id` left false this lowers `gl_GlobalInvocationID` into workgroup/local-id arithmetic before SSBO offsets are built. This whitelist only accepts the pre-lowering global-invocation intrinsics as equal leaves, so a normal identity/binary map prepared by that pipeline can now fail the new offset gate and fall through instead of being replayed; either run this detector before that lowering or teach the walker the lowered workgroup/local-id roots.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include offset_shift in byte-offset equality**

This compares only the offset SSA expression, but NIR SSBO load/store byte addresses also include the intrinsic `offset_shift` metadata (`(offset + base) << offset_shift`). If a matched load and store have the same source expression with different shifts, this gate still reports equality and the fullscreen replay can admit a kernel whose load and store byte offsets differ; compare the load/store `nir_intrinsic_offset_shift` values or fold the shift into the scalar comparison before setting `offset_eq`.

nodes.body: The evidence-tier section reserves “proven” for Rocq-formally-verified claims, but this sentence reads like the *transform kernels themselves* are “proven.” Later paragraphs clarify trust boundaries, but tightening the opening wording here would prevent misreading (i.e., only the algebra is proven).

Since the evidence-tier section already points to `open_gororoba` and its `proofs/theories/*.v`, it would be clearer to qualify these as `open_gororoba` paths.

“hand translation of that verified extraction” is easy to misread as the extraction process being verified. Given the preceding sentence explicitly states there is no verified extraction backend, it would be clearer to describe this as a hand translation of the *extracted OCaml*, and to name the shader path consistently as the R2VB producer (not “r300 producer”).

“Qm.f” is introduced here without a definition elsewhere in this document. Adding a short parenthetical (fixed-point with m integer bits and f fractional bits) would make the FP24 exact-integer window constraint self-contained.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep FP24 exactness tied to accumulator bounds**

When this design is used to admit generic Qm.f vertex kernels, `m + f <= 17` only bounds each fixed-point value inside the FP24 integer window; a multiply or DP4 can still produce products/sums above that window. The existing r300 numeric-domain comments use per-kernel bounds such as `4*(2^7-1)^2 < 2^17` and mark wider U8 dots approximate, so saying this closes the trust boundary for all such vertex math would misclassify non-exact transforms as proven. Please narrow this to the theorem's actual operand/accumulator range or require a per-operation result bound.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't treat verified extraction as Rocq-to-C**

For the `rocq-verified-extraction` branch of this future path, the project targets Rocq-to-OCaml/Malfunction rather than C, so installing it would not collapse the hand translation boundary for an r300 C kernel; it would leave a separate OCaml/Malfunction-to-C rewrite or compiler boundary outside the proof. This matters when someone chooses the future toolchain from this design doc; keep CertiCoq as the C/Clight option and describe verified extraction as an OCaml-side option.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require unit quaternions for rotation proofs**

When the input quaternion is not normalized, the sandwich `q*v*conj(q)` scales by `|q|^2`; it is a pure rotation only for unit `q` (or when using `q*v*inverse(q)`). The existing r300 QROTATE theorem text carries that unit precondition, so this proof recipe needs to record the same normalization requirement or a non-unit kernel could be stamped as a proven rotation while producing scaled vertices.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve loop-header phi values before overwriting**

When the taken predecessor is a loop backedge, NIR can legally use another phi in the same destination block as a phi source because the loop header dominates the latch. Copying each phi directly into its destination while iterating the block serializes what should be parallel copies; a loop that swaps two carried values such as `a = phi(a0, b)` and `b = phi(b0, a)` will set both to old `b` on re-entry. This makes the direct-NIR executor produce wrong vertex results for valid loop-carried SSA, so stage all selected phi sources before writing any phi destinations for the block.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct the R2VB POW-lowering claim**

For the R2VB lighting path, a specular term introduced as `nir_op_fpow` is not automatically lowered just because the shader is later compiled as a fragment shader: `r300_r2vb_restage_vs_as_fs` clones the VS NIR and only changes `info.stage`, while `r300_r2vb.c` still admits `nir_op_fpow`; downstream `nir_to_rc.c` emits `RC_OPCODE_POW`, and the R300 fragment emitter has no POW case. So a restaged or driver-synthesized lighting kernel with `pow(N.H, s)` can pass the policy/classifier but fail or dummy out at fragment compile time unless the implementation explicitly runs lowering or builds EX2/LG2 itself.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve GL attenuation coefficients**

This row only covers inverse-square attenuation, but Mesa's fixed-function vertex generator implements the GL formula as `1 / dot(vec3(1, d, d*d), attenuation)` (`src/mesa/main/ffvertex_prog.c`, which cites GL 2.1 formula 2.4). If HBTCL-06 is used as the implementation map, any light with non-default constant or linear attenuation will produce wrong colors even though the required fragment primitive is still just a dot plus `RCP`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add an R2VB-specific overflow route**

For R2VB producer draws, this overflow route is not actually available: `r300_r2vb_emit_producer` emits its own `DRAW_IMMD` command stream, while the `R300_FS_MULTIPASS` wrapper only runs from the normal `r300_render.c` draw path after it sees `multipass_pass_b`. A lighting producer that exceeds 64 slots will therefore either remain failed or run only the pass-A code into the vertex BO, and this document already says R400_US is not wired into `r300_r2vb.c`, so this should be recorded as future R2VB work rather than a usable fallback.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the GL LIT clamps in the lighting map**

The table says the standard lighting kernel has no missing primitive, but the GL fixed-function path does not use raw `N.L` and raw `pow(N.H, s)`: Mesa's `emit_lit` clamps diffuse/specular dot products and suppresses specular when `N.L <= 0`. If this policy is used as the implementation checklist, back-facing or negatively lit vertices can still receive diffuse/specular contributions unless the fragment-ALU plan explicitly includes those `MAX`/compare/CMP terms.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count ROUND as a lowered sequence**

This overstates the native RS482 fragment opcode set: `radeon_program_alu.c` documents that the R300/R500 fragment ALU has `FRC` but no `ROUND`, and lowers `ROUND` to an add/FRC/add sequence. Any lighting or sin/cos range-reduction budget that treats `ROUND` as one native slot will undercount the 64-ALU limit this section is trying to police.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body: The sentence "All values are FP24" reads as if it applies to every value in the pipeline (including app-provided attributes). In context this section is describing the coordinate contract, so it would be clearer/less error-prone to scope FP24 to the coordinate values represented in this table.

This table row uses the shorthand `VTE_CNTL`, but elsewhere in the document (including a few lines below) the register is named `VAP_VTE_CNTL`. Using the full register name here avoids ambiguity and keeps the contract self-contained.

The prose refers to the "`VTE_CNTL` flip" even though the actual register is `VAP_VTE_CNTL` (as used in the previous sections and the sentence right above). Consider using `VAP_VTE_CNTL` here to keep terminology consistent.

The first bullet enumerates only `VTX_XY_FMT` and `VTX_Z_FMT`, but earlier the document frames the bypass space selection as `VTX_XY_FMT`/`VTX_Z_FMT`/`VTX_W0_FMT` collectively. Using the same `VTX_*_FMT` shorthand here avoids looking like an incomplete/partial register recipe.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Document the VTE reciprocal path**

This makes HBTCL-04 treat a software perspective divide as mandatory before any VAP handoff, but the R3xx/R5xx VTE register docs and the existing r300 viewport state use the setup engine for that reciprocal: the hardware path programs `R300_VTX_W0_FMT | VPORT_*_ENA` while leaving `VTX_XY_FMT`/`VTX_Z_FMT` clear, and `r300_render.c`'s RS482 direct-VB path emits that same shape for clip-space vertices. If future work follows this contract, clip-space re-ingest is incorrectly ruled out and HBTCL-04 will implement an extra SW divide instead of validating the existing VTE `1/w` path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve application position w**

For draws whose position input is a four-component attribute with `w != 1`, this contract drops the app-provided homogeneous coordinate before the MVP multiply. The current R2VB MVP path only defaults `w` to 1 when the source format has fewer than four components (`comps > 3 ? v[3] : 1.0f`), so following this table would change clip coordinates and then clipping/divide results for valid vec4 position inputs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Feed object attributes through the producer**

For the fragment-ALU MVP path, `3D_LOAD_VBPNTR` is the VAP re-ingest mechanism, not how the producer shader receives object-space attributes: the current `r300_r2vb_emit_producer` path supplies them as embedded `DRAW_IMMD` data, and the later plan points future producer-side fetches at texture/TAM. If HBTCL-04 follows this row, it wires the app VBO into the bypass VAP instead of into the fragment producer, so the MVP stage will not consume the object vertices it is supposed to transform.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body: r300_r2vb_divide_enabled() treats any presence of R300_R2VB_DIVIDE as enabled, so `R300_R2VB_DIVIDE=0` still turns the feature on. This file’s other gates consistently require an explicit opt-in value (e.g. "1"); matching that avoids surprising behavior and makes it possible to disable the gate without unsetting the variable.

r2vb_divide_position() bakes viewport scale/translate as NIR immediates (nir_imm_float(vp->scale/translate)). That makes the viewport effectively fixed at shader-build time. In the externals path, r300_r2vb_get_transform_fs() caches the transform FS on the context, so subsequent draws (or tests) that change r300->viewport will keep using stale baked values, while the verification path reads the live r300->viewport. Consider making viewport parameters dynamic (UBO/push constants updated per draw) or invalidating/rebuilding the cached FS when the viewport state changes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bypass the HW viewport when DIVIDE emits window coords**

With `R300_R2VB_DIVIDE=1` and a real MVP submit, this code writes window-space xyz into the clip BO, but `r300_r2vb_exec_mvp_draw` still re-ingests that BO through `r300_r2vb_exec_passthrough_draw`, which unconditionally emits `SE_VPORT_*` and `VAP_VTE_CNTL` with `R300_VPORT_*_ENA` at `src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_render.c:1446-1451` for clip-space inputs. For any non-identity viewport, the producer's viewport MAD is applied once here and then again by the VAP, so the BO verifier can pass while the rendered draw lands at the wrong window coordinates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebuild cached DIVIDE FS when the viewport changes**

In `R300_R2VB_MVP_EXTERNALS=1` this builder is cached on `r300->r2vb_transform_fs` (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_r2vb.c:205-206`); after this call, `r2vb_divide_position` turns `vp->scale/translate` into `nir_imm_float` constants, while only the matrix rows are loaded from the per-draw constant buffer. If the application changes viewport after the first DIVIDE draw, later draws reuse the old scale/bias in the cached FS but the CPU verifier and expected output use the current `r300->viewport`, so externals mode renders/verifies against stale coordinates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require an exact opt-in for DIVIDE**

This gate treats any exported value as enabled, so common attempts to disable the experiment with `R300_R2VB_DIVIDE=0` or an empty value still make the producer emit divided/window-space positions. The neighboring route gates parse an exact `"1"` opt-in, and this behavior-changing path should do the same so stale environment or config does not silently change the experimental render and verifier outputs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict DIVIDE_VERIFY to MVP-shaped position shaders**

Under `R300_R2VB_RESTAGE=1`, `r300_r2vb_route_mvp` admits any straight-line fragment-aluable VS, but this new verifier always calls `r2vb_verify_window_readback`, whose reference is hard-coded to `clip = cols * model`. For a restaged non-MVP position kernel, the producer can be correct while `R300_R2VB_DIVIDE_VERIFY=1` reports mismatches against the wrong CPU oracle; gate this verifier to `r300_vs_is_mvp` or dispatch to the shader-specific oracle.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace internal HBTCL labels in comments**

The new source comment names the gate and validation path with `HBTCL-04b`/`HBTCL-04g`; the repository instructions require source comments to stand on mechanism and testable behavior without internal task or phase labels. These labels also recur in the added comments, so a maintainer cannot resolve the authority from the source alone; replace them with the actual mechanism, public test, or oracle description.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Charge DIVIDE ALU against the restage ceiling**

With `R300_R2VB_DIVIDE=1`, the restage classifier still admits shaders based on the original VS ALU count in `r300_vs_nir_is_fragment_aluable`, but these extra divide/viewport instructions are inserted afterward. A shader close to the 64-slot R300 fragment limit can pass the gate and then compile the producer as a dummy/error shader or overflow the hardware budget, so the classifier needs to reserve or count the divide sequence when the gate is active.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body: r2vb_clip_classify_readback() maps the producer BO with `box.width = count * 16`; when `count == 0` this becomes a zero-sized map, but elsewhere in this function the code explicitly avoids zero-sized maps (uses `(count ? count : 1) * 16`). This should be consistent to avoid map failures/assertions on empty draws.

The clip-classification path assumes the earlier "two-submit flush + map" ordering happened before CPU readback, but that ordering is skipped when `R300_R2VB_MVP_SINGLECS=1` (`single_cs` mode). With both env vars enabled, this can read stale/uninitialized producer data and produce misleading classification output.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for the producer before classifying the BO**

When `R300_R2VB_CLIP_CLASSIFY=1`, this maps the clip BO after `r300->context.flush(..., NULL, 0)`, but `r300_buffer_transfer_map` forces every read map to `PIPE_MAP_UNSYNCHRONIZED` before calling the winsys map, so this read does not wait for the producer's color-buffer write to retire. On an asynchronous GPU submit, the oracle can classify stale pooled BO contents instead of the actual FP24 output; add an explicit fence or winsys buffer wait before reading.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip divide verification under clip classification**

When `R300_R2VB_CLIP_CLASSIFY=1` is combined with `R300_R2VB_DIVIDE=1` and `R300_R2VB_DIVIDE_VERIFY=1`, this forces the producer to write clip-space coordinates, but the later divide-verify block still interprets the same BO as window-space and compares it against the CPU divide+viewport reference. That makes the diagnostic report false mismatches before the clip classifier runs; the divide verifier should be suppressed or keyed off the actual `produced_space`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore app atoms before falling back**

When `R300_R2VB_CLIP_CLASSIFY=1`, this returns to the gallivm fallback immediately after the producer pass, but `r300_r2vb_emit_producer` hand-emits framebuffer, scissor, viewport, ZB, rasterizer, and clip registers outside the atom system; the later re-ingest path explicitly dirties those atoms before drawing for this reason. Without the same dirtying here, the fallback draw can reuse the producer's one-row color target/scissor or `CLIP_DISABLE` state instead of the application's state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect Draw clip flags in the oracle**

When the rasterizer disables Z clipping or enables user clip planes/clip distances, Draw does not use this unconditional six-plane hardwired mask: `draw_update_clip_flags` gates Z clipping on `depth_clip_near`, and `draw_cliptest_tmp.h` adds `DO_CLIP_USER` planes. Calling `r300_r2vb_clipcode` here can therefore report false reject/partial results for depth-clamp draws, or false accepts for primitives clipped only by user planes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore FS constants before the fallback**

When `R300_R2VB_CLIP_CLASSIFY=1` is used with `R300_R2VB_MVP_EXTERNALS=1` or `R300_R2VB_RESTAGE=1`, the producer setup overwrites fragment constant buffer 0 with the transform matrix and then this path falls back to gallivm without restoring the application's FS constants. If the fallback fragment shader reads uniforms, the diagnostic changes the rendered frame even though the gate is documented as classification-only.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body: The summary line in r2vb_clip_classify_readback is printed unconditionally. For the clip-route path this adds per-draw logging even when diagnostics are not requested; gate it behind R300_R2VB_CLIP_CLASSIFY to keep clip-route usable without log spam.

r2vb_run_transform_producer relies on a flush+map-for-read to enforce ordering/coherency for the produced BO, but it currently ignores a failed map and still reports success. If buffer_map fails, the subsequent re-ingest can read stale data; treat map failure as a hard fallback and ensure fixed-function state is re-emitted on the next draw.

In the clip-route early-exit paths (unsupported/fallback or whole-draw reject), the code returns to normal rendering without re-ingest. The producer wrote scissor/clip/raster/FB/ZB registers directly (outside the atom system), so those values can leak into subsequent draws unless the owning atoms are marked dirty before returning.

r2vb_clip_classify_readback is now used as part of the clip-route decision, but it prints one line per vertex unconditionally. For large draws this can be a major perf hit and log spam when R300_R2VB_CLIP_ROUTE is enabled; keep the per-vertex dump behind the existing R300_R2VB_CLIP_CLASSIFY diagnostic gate.

r2vb_clip_classify_readback currently prints one line per triangle unconditionally (prim/or/and/class). Under the new clip-route action this can explode stderr output; gate the per-primitive print behind R300_R2VB_CLIP_CLASSIFY so clip-route can run without verbose diagnostics.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Dirty producer state before clip-route fallback**

With `R300_R2VB_CLIP_ROUTE=1`, this fallback is reached after the clip-space producer has already hand-written framebuffer/scissor/viewport/ZB/RS registers. The normal re-ingest path later marks those atoms dirty before drawing again, but this early return falls through to gallivm while the driver can still believe the app atoms are clean, so partial or unsupported draws can render through the producer clip target, one-row scissor, or `CLIP_DISABLE`. Dirty or restore the same atoms before returning, including the consume return below.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail when the window producer cannot be prepared**

On the clip-route accept path this helper is called a second time after `r2vb_produced_space` is switched to `WINDOW`; if `r300_r2vb_prepare_states()` returns false here, no window-space BO is emitted, but the helper still returns true and the caller later fetches the previous clip-space BO with `r2vb_source_window` set. That renders clip coordinates as already-window coordinates instead of falling back, so the helper should return false when preparation fails.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Synchronize before classifying in single-CS mode**

When `R300_R2VB_CLIP_ROUTE=1` is combined with `R300_R2VB_MVP_SINGLECS=1`, the producer above deliberately skips the flush/map synchronization, but this CPU readback still classifies the BO immediately. `r300_buffer_transfer_map()` makes read maps `PIPE_MAP_UNSYNCHRONIZED`, so the map does not submit or wait for the pending producer CS; on a recycled BO this can classify stale contents and incorrectly deliver or consume the draw. Force a synchronized read for the classify pass, or reject single-CS for this route.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body: r300_r2vb_clip_triangle accepts num_attrs but never bounds-checks it against R300_R2VB_CLIP_MAX_ATTRS, so a caller passing a larger value would write past the attr[][] array in r300_r2vb_clip_lerp(). Clamp (or assert) num_attrs before using it to avoid a latent out-of-bounds write.

r2vb_clip_build_clipped_list leaves *out_model unchanged on error paths (e.g., map failure). The current caller initializes cmodel to NULL, but making the callee always initialize the out-parameter avoids future misuse and makes the API contract clearer.

**issue (bug_risk):** Primitive restart handling relies on post-bias index values; this may diverge from draw_vbo semantics.

In `r2vb_topology_gather_indices`, restart detection uses:
```c
bool is_restart = info->primitive_restart && info->index_size != 0 &&
                  i < n_verts && src[i] == info->restart_index;
```
where `src[i]` has already had `draw->index_bias` applied:
```c
src[i] = (uint32_t)((int64_t)raw + draw->index_bias);
```
If `restart_index` is defined in the pre-bias index space (as in `draw_vbo`), this comparison will fail whenever `index_bias != 0`, causing restart markers to be ignored and strips/fans to be incorrectly stitched. Please confirm the intended semantics and, if needed, compare `raw` to `restart_index` before applying the bias.

✅ Addressed in 577475adf1aa6a0b733bfcc65fbd4ae97466a05f: Restart detection now compares the raw index value (`src[i]`) to `restart_index` before applying `index_bias`, and the bias is only added when emitting `gidx`, aligning the semantics with `draw_vbo`.

When R300_R2VB_TOPOLOGY is enabled, r2vb_topology_gather_indices allocates `src` sized to `draw->count` before enforcing the 4096-vertex producer ceiling. A large draw->count can cause a very large temporary allocation even though the gather will inevitably overflow and return false once the output hits the 4096 cap.

Primitive-restart detection compares the *bias-adjusted* `src[i]` against `info->restart_index` directly. Gallium’s restart semantics compare the raw index value to `restart_index` (no bias) (see `src/gallium/auxiliary/draw/draw_pt.c:390`), so with a non-zero `draw->index_bias` this code won’t detect restart indices and will generate triangles across restart boundaries.

The comment says `info->restart_index` is "post index_bias", but Gallium’s primitive restart index is defined in the raw index stream (before applying `draw->index_bias`) and the code is intended to split on that raw value.

nodes.body: r300_r2vb_restore_app_fs_consts() is a no-op when fs_const0_app.valid is false, so an R2VB producer that bound the matrix into FS const0 can leak that binding into subsequent application draws (and future FS variant selection will still see the producer matrix as the live constant source). It should actively restore the "no const0 bound" state when the mirror is invalid, e.g. by calling set_constant_buffer(..., NULL) once r300_set_constant_buffer handles NULL as an unbind.

r300_set_constant_buffer() treats a NULL/empty constant buffer as a no-op and returns without clearing the currently bound constants. With the new R2VB producer path, this makes it impossible to restore the "no FS const0 bound" state (and leaves whatever producer data was last bound visible to subsequent FS variant keying). Handle NULL/empty for FS const0 as an explicit unbind by clearing the stored pointer and marking fs_constants dirty.
